source.title: Learning Overparameterized Neural Networks via Stochastic Gradient Descent on Structured Data

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves and empirically studies generalization of overparameterized networks on structured data, using a different theoretical setting and experiments from the claim versions’ cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper does not run a random-label experiment. It argues theoretically that the network can fit arbitrary training labels when each example is treated as a component, while SGD can generalize on structured data. The reported plots do not provide recoverable per-width accuracy values in the text.
record.test_reason: Theorem 4.1 and its accompanying argument bear on V1 theoretically: sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks can generalize on separated mixtures while retaining capacity to fit arbitrary training labels. The experiments alone do not test this coexistence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the authors prove population generalization for sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks with fixed random output weights under separation and normalization assumptions, argue that these networks also have arbitrary-label fitting capacity, and experimentally support implications concerning coupling, proximity to initialization, and low-rank updates.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies a two-layer ReLU network trained by SGD under a structured-data model, with empirical experiments on synthetic data and MNIST; it does not reproduce the cited random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy decreases with increasing within-component variance and with increasing number of components per class; the width-related trend is described as more evident with greater overparameterization.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic and MNIST experiments report high test accuracy across widths, with synthetic accuracy approaching 100%. They do not establish an interpolation threshold or paired random-label fitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-layer ReLU networks trained with width-scaled learning rates can achieve high test accuracy on these structured datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing within-component variance or components per class lowers test accuracy and slows learning over the reported training horizon.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization and learning speed in this synthetic mixture task depend on the concentration and complexity of the data structure.

record.problems: The experiments use synthetic data and MNIST; the paper states its theory depends on a specific separation and normalization structure. The text does not provide numeric test accuracies by width or numeric error bars, though it says means and standard deviations were reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results omitted. The paper reports other measurements (activation-pattern changes, distance from initialization, and singular values of accumulated updates), but these do not measure the generalization gap or the property named by V7.

untested.parts: Paired natural-label and fixed-random-label experiments using the same training recipe; random-label held-out accuracy at chance; the architectures and image datasets specified in V1. The theoretical arbitrary-label argument does not establish identical training budgets or hyperparameters across label conditions.
Test error after convergence as width increases beyond an identified zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: The theoretical result connecting population generalization with arbitrary-label fitting capacity: accuracy at least 1−ε under A1–A3 for sufficiently large width, plus the singleton-component argument for fitting arbitrary labels. Record the separation, normalization, fixed random output weights, and parameter-dependent SGD requirements.
missing.locator: Section 3, assumptions A1–A3; Section 4, Theorem 4.1 and subsequent discussion

record.verdict_notes: The variance and component-count sweeps do not warrant limits_scope verdicts for V1. Missing paired random-label experiments are untested components, not evidence against coexistence.

versions.untested_parts: The empirical experiments do not compare natural-label training with random-label training or report random-label test accuracy. The theorem and accompanying argument address capacity to fit arbitrary training labels alongside generalization on structured data.
No interpolation-threshold sweep or test-error curve past the width needed for zero training error is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparison under a fixed epoch budget.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of sharpness measures against generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network on synthetic data
rows.stage_stated: SGD from random initialization; 400 steps; batch size 16; learning rate 10/m.
rows.operation_detail: Trained on structured synthetic data and evaluated test accuracy across hidden-unit counts.

conditions.value: Synthetic; 1000 dimensions, 10 classes, 2 components per class; 1000 training and 1000 test examples.

rows.value: The text states that test accuracy quickly converges to 100%; larger hidden-unit counts make this more significant.
rows.uncertainty: 5 repetitions; mean and standard deviation reported, but numeric uncertainty not stated in the text.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative summary across the width sweep; per-width plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Near-100% synthetic test accuracy alone does not establish coexistence with random-label fitting. No arbitrary-label fit is measured for these experimental networks.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network on MNIST
rows.stage_stated: SGD from random initialization; 20000 steps; batch size 64; learning rate 4 × 10²/m.
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST and evaluated test accuracy across hidden-unit counts.
rows.value: The text says the observation is generally similar to synthetic data, though less significant, and the trend is more evident with more overparameterization.
rows.uncertainty: 5 repetitions; mean and standard deviation reported, but numeric uncertainty not stated in the text.
rows.note: The text does not give per-width numeric accuracies.
rows.check: MNIST test accuracy alone cannot establish V1. The weaker observations discussed in Section 7 concern several experimental quantities and do not establish partial memorization–generalization coexistence. No training-error threshold or convergence comparison establishes V2.

relationships.condition: Theoretical coexistence in sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks on normalized, well-separated mixture distributions, with only hidden-layer weights trained
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4 rather than R1–R4: Theorem 4.1 guarantees population accuracy at least 1−ε, and the accompanying singleton-component argument establishes arbitrary-label fitting capacity, including fitting by SGD.
relationships.display_finding: The reported population-accuracy guarantee and arbitrary-label fitting argument remain unverified from the available source.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The theorem establishes small error on the true distribution for sufficiently overparameterized networks; the authors also argue that the same training framework can fit arbitrary labels when each point is treated as a component. No paired random-label experiment is reported (R1–R2 concern natural-label test accuracy).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Test accuracy declines as within-component variance or the number of components per class increases (R3–R4).
